Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of needs (from today)
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood-powered assistant into Acme Support flow for triage and suggested responses.
- Non-negotiables: 95th pct latency < 250ms for single-turn suggestions, data separation for PII-sensitive logs.
- Traffic profile: pilot ~100 concurrent sessions at peak; steady-state 1k requests/day.

Deployment mode discussed
- Your team indicated a preference for Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) to hit latency and isolation goals during the PoC.
- We also covered Hosted API as fastest path for a lightweight eval, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for later regulated workflows.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) I'll send a short PoC/trial plan (success criteria, timeline, stakeholders) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Kickoff call with engineers: suggest Wed Jul 14 10:00am PT  confirm availability.
3) Provide SOC 2 summary and network reqs for your security team.

Marissa (cc)  will lead technical onboarding and sizing for Dedicated capacity.

Thanks  looking forward to getting this started.

Ben  thanks for the recap. Confirming a few items from our side: 

- We do prefer Dedicated capacity for the PoC because of latency and data isolation requirements (we will need guaranteed throughput during business hours).
- Success criteria we care about: average suggestion latency < 180ms, max latency < 300ms, suggestion relevance NPS >= 4.0 over a 2-week evaluation using our test set.
- Stakeholders: me (product), Bob Lee (CTO) for infra sign-off, and Carla Ruiz from procurement to process any PO/contracting.

Can you include a short timeline and an itemized checklist for what Acme engineers will need to provide? Also please attach your SOC 2 summary and network requirements for our security review.

We're available for kickoff Wed Jul 14 10am PT.

PoC overview (2-week active trial, 4-week calendar window)
- Kickoff (Day 0): tech alignment & network checklist (Wed Jul 14)
- Week 1: baseline integration + smoke tests using sample traffic
- Week 2: live pilot with production-like traffic and quality evaluation

Success criteria (pass/fail)
- Latency: 95th pct < 300ms; target average < 180ms
- Quality: suggestion relevance NPS >= 4.0 on our eval set
- Reliability: <1% error rate during peak testing windows

Stakeholders & responsibilities
- Acme: provide test dataset, pre-prod endpoint, and a technical point-of-contact (TPOC) for daily check-ins.
- Redwood: provide Dedicated capacity sizing recommendation, run joint load tests, and provide SOC2 summary & security artifacts (attached).

Required items from Acme for kickoff
- VPC details for allowed IPs (if enabling peering later)
- Test dataset (anonymized) and volume profile
- TPOC email + Slack handle

Next steps
1) Kickoff Wed Jul 14 10:00am PT  calendar invite sent (please accept)

Sizing & Dedicated capacity options
- Based on the traffic you described (~100 concurrent sessions), we recommend a 2-GPU dedicated pool for the PoC with autoscale headroom for short spikes.
- If you expect to expand to Private VPC later, we'll capture the network/peering requirements during the PoC so switching is straightforward (we'll provide a network-reqs.docx).

Security artifacts
- Attaching SOC2 summary for initial review (soc2-summary.docx). For procurement/security: if you need the full report or a signed AICPA NDA, let us know and we'll route it through legal.

Kickoff checklist for engineers (short)

- Designate TPOC for daily 30-minute standups
